answer: A copper latency floor ties each identity to a minimum inter-arrival interval, so bursts reveal coordinated creation. The rule rejects any cluster whose request timing is tighter than the velvet baseline of organic signups observed over the prior week. An attacker must therefore rent genuine overnight quiet, pacing clones across an oasis of idle hours to imitate human rhythm. That pacing cost scales linearly with clone count and delays each wave by days, making mass registration slow and expensive.
